subject.title: Session modelOverride persists across gateway restarts, silently overrides config default

question: Should explicit or legacy user model overrides survive `/new`, `/reset`, and gateway restarts after config default changes, and should OpenClaw add a scoped bulk reset/reconcile command for clearing them?
rationale: Current code intentionally preserves user/legacy pins and documents `/model default` for per-session clearing, while the requested automatic or bulk behavior affects compatibility-sensitive persisted session and provider-routing state.

options.title: Add opt-in reset/reconcile
options.body: Preserve explicit pins by default, add dry-run reporting, and require scoped flags or commands to clear selected session/model/auth pins.

options.title: Change reset precedence
options.body: Make `/new`, `/reset`, or restart discard explicit session model pins so config defaults take over, accepting a compatibility break for durable user selections.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Leave `/model default`, status visibility, and doctor warnings as the supported recovery path and close the remaining bulk-reset request as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in reset/reconcile
recommendation.body: Preserve explicit pins by default, add dry-run reporting, and require scoped flags or commands to clear selected session/model/auth pins.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the broadest observed history across status, model override, and session-state behavior and is a likely decision owner for compatibility semantics.
